newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bomb kills eight, militants detained in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills eight, militants detained in Pakistan.

text.p: Eight people were killed and 21 wounded when an early morning bomb blast tore through a bus near the Pakistani city of Sialkot, in Punjab province, on Monday, police said.
They said nine seriously wounded passengers were being treated at Sialkot's Allama Iqbal Hospital.
The explosion occurred at 6:15 a.m. (0115 GMT) in a bus travelling to Sialkot from Lakhanal near the Indian border. Many of the passengers were day labourers, hospital doctors said.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the blast and no word on its motive.
Police picked up about 500 Sunni and Shi'ite Moslem militants in Punjab province overnight as part of efforts to quell a wave of sectarian unrest, officials in Lahore said.
More than 400 were released after questioning and 92 were detained for further investigation, they said.
The Punjab provincial government ordered the crackdown, which began at midnight (1900 GMT Sunday), following a spate of killings involving rival religious groups.

In the latest attacks, gunmen killed at least five people, four of them in a mosque, in Lahore on Sunday. A Shi'ite lawyer was shot and wounded in the arm in the southern Punjab town of Dera Ghazi Khan on Monday, local officials said.

The activists detained overnight included members of the Sunni Moslem Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) organisation and two Shi'ite Moslem groups, Sipah-i-Mohammad Pakistan (SMP) and Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan (TJP), officials and relatives said.
The Punjab provincial government said on Sunday it would seize all literature deemed liable to fan sectarian prejudices.

Sectarian violence is rife in Punjab, where militant Sunni and Shi'ite factions are engaged in a feud that officials say has killed more than 100 people so far this year, including religious scholars, lawyers and doctors.
